correctness.rationale: For six points, local residue cardinalities force no repeated classes modulo any prime norm≥6 or the squares of the only small primes norm3 and norm4. Unique ideal factorization restricts every pair difference to norm 1,3,4,12. All 24 possible nonzero vectors are exhaustively listed, so testing 24 choose 5 subsets is logically complete. Exactly 54 pair-compatible sets form three symmetry orbits; all violate first-power balance modulo 3 or 4, with certified profiles. Four direct small witnesses satisfy all prime-power balances. General n+2 existence theorem gives the seven-point minimum.

originality.rationale: Full-text statements in 2011 Petrov–Volkov and 2015 Byszewski–Frączyk–Szumowicz give Gaussian small-degree behavior, general local criteria, asymptotic quadratic nonexistence, and the n+2 universal upper bound. They do not determine the first obstruction n=5 over Z[omega]. New exhaustive 54-configuration arithmetic obstruction yields the precise degree-five minimum seven. value.rationale: The exact first nonexistence threshold in the Eisenstein integer ring and the minimal size seven of degree-five universal interpolation sets are natural discrete invariants of arithmetic rings. General asymptotic nonexistence in imaginary quadratic fields and Gaussian low-degree behavior leave these specific natural questions open; the 3-versus-4 prime-ideal profile obstruction explains the failure structurally.
